structured_output.hypothesis: In North Sea plaice, Fulton's condition factor K = 100*W/L^3, averaged per 1-cm length class, rises with length to a single interior maximum near 30 cm and then declines slowly at larger sizes.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using individual fish records (length in cm, individual weight in g) from DATRAS plaice (Pleuronectes platessa) with 1-cm length classes of n>=30 fish, pooled over sexes and surveys: (a) the 3-class moving-average of mean K peaks at a length between 25 and 35 cm; (b) mean K at the peak exceeds mean K in the 10-15 cm classes by at least 5% and exceeds mean K in classes of 45 cm and larger by at least 3%; (c) in at least 90% of 1000 bootstrap resamples of fish the peak falls in 25-35 cm.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if any of the following holds: the smoothed peak lies outside 25-35 cm; mean K at 45+ cm is not at least 3% below the peak; K at the peak is less than 5% above K at 10-15 cm; K is monotone with no interior maximum; or fewer than 90% of bootstrap resamples place the peak in 25-35 cm. If fewer than 5000 fish have both length and weight, the test is declared inconclusive rather than passed or failed.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's k = W/L^3 is the condition factor (Fulton's K), here scaled by 100 with W in g and L in cm. His data were early-20th-century North Sea plaice from fishery investigations. His 'size at which sexual maturity begins' of about 30 cm is taken as given and not tested; the test concerns only the existence and location of the interior K maximum and the slow decline after it. Modern reinterpretation: contemporary North Sea survey trawl data stand in for his historical samples. Seasonal confounding from gonad weight is handled by analyzing each survey quarter separately as a sensitivity check, with the pooled result as primary. Fields used: species (Pleuronectes platessa), length class (LngtClass with length code to convert to cm), individual weight (IndWgt), sex, maturity, survey, quarter, year, from the DATRAS biological (CA) exchange data.

dataset.name: ICES DATRAS (Database of Trawl Surveys)
dataset.publisher: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)
dataset.why_it_fits: DATRAS provides open downloads and web services for North Sea trawl survey biological records (e.g. NS-IBTS, BTS) including individual length, individual weight, sex and maturity for plaice, allowing K by length class to be computed directly. Individual weight coverage for plaice varies by survey and year and must be checked before analysis.
